title: Just-open streak
intro: Opening the app before your chosen hour is a streak of its own.

title: If-then plans
intro: Decide in advance. The app reminds you at the time you pick, with a Start button.

title: Habit stacking
intro: Attach a session to something you already do every day, like morning tea or the college bus.

title: Temptation bundling
intro: Save a link to a favourite playlist. The play button shows only on the running timer, so the music belongs to work.

title: Ugly first draft
intro: Perfectionism cannot survive this goal.
task: Make it bad on purpose. Ugly counts.

title: Setup-only session
intro: No work required. Only get ready to work.
task: Open the files and clear the desk. Nothing else.

title: Dice start
intro: Cannot choose? Let the dice pick among up to three of your tasks.

title: Bad-day bar
intro: Rough day? Drop today's door to one minute. One minute still counts as a full win and keeps every streak.
setLabel: Today is a rough day: 1 minute is enough

title: Home-screen widget
body: Long-press your home screen, choose Widgets, find Challenger Timer and drop "Start 2 min" anywhere. It shows your streak and starts a session without opening the app. It turns from red to green once you have worked today.

title: Quick-settings tile
body: Pull down the notification shade twice, tap the pencil, and drag "Start 2 min" into your tiles. One tap there starts a session.

title: Voice start
body: On the Timer tab, tap the microphone and say "Start five minutes on DSA". It understands a number of minutes and a project name. Needs the phone's speech recogniser.

title: NFC desk tag
body: Write the link challengertimer://start to an NFC sticker with any free NFC writer app, and stick it on your desk. Tapping the phone on it starts a 2-minute session.

title: Arrived at my study place
intro: Automatic location detection is not built. This is the manual version: tap when you sit down at the library, lab or desk.
task: I just sat down. Open the first thing.

title: Charger cue
intro: Plugging the phone in offers a start. Android only allows this while the app is still alive in the background, so it will not fire if the app was closed long ago.
setLabel: Offer a start when I plug in

title: Morning first win
intro: Blocks every app (except phone, launcher and settings) until today's first session is finished. Needs Earn your phone switched on in Settings.
setLabel: Block all apps until the first session

title: Start count
intro: Also shown as the biggest number on Home.

title: Full and tiny versions
body: On the Streaks tab, tap a habit's name and give it a tiny version, like "Read one line". On a bad day the TINY button keeps the streak alive.

title: Weekly streaks
body: Some habits do not need to be daily. Tap a habit's name on the Streaks tab and choose "4 of 7 days". Its streak then counts weeks that hit the target.

title: Chain calendar
intro: This month. Every day you showed up is crossed off. A snowflake is a day a freeze covered.

title: Wake-time streak
intro: Tap the button when you get up. It counts if you are up no later than 30 minutes after your target.

title: Phone-free first hour
intro: Self-reported: tick it on days your first waking hour had no phone.

title: Review streak
intro: Counts days you answered the three daily questions (in the Reflection tools).

title: Hard-thing-first streak
intro: Self-reported: tick it on days you did the task you dreaded most before anything else.

title: Stacking bonus
body: Feed three streaks on the same day (for example a session plus two habit ticks) and that day pays an extra 30 XP.

title: Streak wager
intro: Bet some XP that the next 7 days pass without an uncovered miss. Freezes still protect you. Win: you gain the amount. Miss a day with no freeze: you lose it.

title: Active days
intro: Choose days that never count against any streak, for example Sunday. Work on those days still counts.

title: Time-window streaks
body: Tap a habit's name on the Streaks tab and set a window, like 06:00 to 09:00. The habit can then only be ticked inside it.

title: Graduation
body: When a habit runs on its own, tap its name on the Streaks tab and graduate it. It moves to "Maintained" and frees your attention for a new one.

title: Three daily questions
intro: Two minutes in the evening.

title: Earned freezes
body: Every 7 active days in a row earns one extra freeze. Earned freezes do not expire at month end. They show as extra lives on the Streaks tab.

title: Decay, not reset
intro: With this on, a break (two uncovered misses in a row) costs 20% of the streak instead of all of it. Off keeps the standard rule.
setLabel: A break keeps 80% of the streak

title: Comeback bonus
body: The first session after an uncovered miss pays its XP twice. Coming back is rewarded more than never slipping.

title: Repair task
intro: Missed yesterday? Do double the minimum today (4 minutes) and restore it.

title: Sick and travel mode
intro: Pauses every streak. No day counts as a miss while it is on. Use it when you are ill or travelling, not when you are avoiding.

title: Exam mode
intro: During exams, show only the habits you marked as your exam set (open a habit on the Streaks tab to mark it). The others are paused, not broken.

title: Miss autopsy
intro: One tap. No essay, no blame. It only feeds the pattern finder.

title: Fresh-start dates
intro: Mondays, the 1st of a month and your birthday are natural restart days. Home mentions it on those days if the streak needs a restart.

title: Lapse plan
intro: Write it now, while you are calm. Home shows it back to you right after a missed day.
prompts: If I miss a day, I will...

title: Friend test
intro: You are kinder to friends than to yourself. Borrow that.
prompts: What would I say to a friend who missed a day?

title: Archive
intro: Old habits are never deleted. Their streaks stay as proof you can do it.

title: Mood check
intro: One tap. Low-mood days you still worked on turn gold in the heatmap.

title: Pomodoro cycles
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and choose Pomodoro. Four 25-minute rounds with 5-minute breaks run by themselves while the app is open. All rounds share one proof at the end.

title: Flowtime
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and choose Flowtime. The timer counts up. Stop when focus fades and you are offered a break one fifth as long as the work.

title: Ramp ladder
intro: The Home session grows by one minute for each day you work, from 2 up to 60. Switch it off any time to go back to 2 minutes.
setLabel: Grow my daily session by 1 minute a day

title: Hard mode
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and switch on Hard mode before you start. If you leave the app for more than 10 seconds, that session ends without credit. Turning the screen off does not count as leaving.

title: Wander tally
intro: The running timer has a "mind wandered" button.

title: Strict breaks
intro: Breaks end on time. If you come back late, the overrun is counted here.

title: Ambient sounds
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and pick brown noise, a rain-like hiss or white noise. They are generated on the phone, so there is no cafe recording.

title: Marathon day
body: On the Timer tab open "More ways to run it" and choose Marathon day: six 25-minute rounds with enforced 5-minute breaks. Optional, and only on days you choose.

title: Deadline tools
body: On the Plan tab, open a task (the arrow on its right), give it a due date and a rough size. The app then sets your own due date 48 hours early and shows sessions left, a daily quota, a start-by date, a backward plan, what waiting 5 days would cost, and the XP bonus for working early.

title: First-touch rule
intro: Every new task with a due date deserves 5 minutes within 24 hours. Open the task from the Plan tab to do it.

title: Neck-level alarm
intro: You also get one reminder a day at cue time while any deadline is at neck level.

title: Cost-of-delay note
intro: Write what the last all-nighter really cost you. It is shown back to you when you try to postpone a task.
prompts: What did the last-minute rush cost me?

title: Future-self letter
intro: Write as you, on the morning after the deadline, to you now.
prompts: Dear me, it is the morning after. Here is what I wish you would do today:

title: Load calendar
intro: The next 8 weeks by how much is due. Three or more due dates in one week are flagged.

title: Deadline post-mortem
intro: Three lines after each deadline. No judgement, only data for next time.
